title: Classic Hot Fudge Sundae
summary: Vanilla ice cream under a quick, glossy homemade hot fudge sauce, softly whipped cream and a cherry on top.

ingredients.item: light corn syrup or glucose syrup
fine sea salt or table salt
vanilla ice cream (8 scoops), bought or homemade
ingredients.note: our French-style vanilla custard ice cream works well

ingredients.item: cherries with stems (fresh, or jarred cherries in syrup)

steps.title: Chill the bowls
steps.text: Put the sundae bowls or glasses in the freezer for 15 min. Cold bowls keep the ice cream from melting the moment it lands.

steps.title: Melt the fudge
steps.text: Put the chocolate, corn syrup, water, sugar, cocoa, butter and salt in the saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir with the spatula until everything has melted into a smooth sauce.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium and let the sauce bubble gently for 3 min, stirring often, until glossy and slightly thicker. Take it off the heat, stir in the vanilla and leave for about 10 min until warm rather than hot. It thickens further as it cools.

steps.title: Whip the cream
steps.text: Whisk the cold cream with the sugar until it forms soft, billowy peaks. Stop there: over-whipped cream turns grainy.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Put two scoops of ice cream in each cold bowl and spoon over the warm fudge. Add a generous spoonful of whipped cream, top with a cherry and serve straight away.

tips: Serve the fudge warm, not boiling hot, so it clings to the ice cream instead of melting it.
Leftover fudge keeps in the fridge for 2 weeks; rewarm gently in short bursts in the microwave.
safety: Add chopped toasted nuts if you like, but remember to tell anyone with a nut allergy.
storage: Assemble sundaes just before serving. Keep leftover fudge sauce covered in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
